Fun little cutesey hacking game that uses a very authentic command line enviornment. If you know your way around a Linux command line this game will be a lot easier for you. People with no command line experience at all might have a hard time learning and remembering the basics, though.

The hacking itself feels pretty 'real', I guess. You have to type commands to run programs and stuff, which all adds to the realism. Sadly the hacking gets repetitive pretty quickly. Even though you get to use different programs as the game progresses, all you're really doing is just typing different stuff. There is a certain clever element to the game though. It will not hold your hand throughout any of the puzzles and it is possible to get properly stuck and have to look up guides online.

A cute little game that is fun to mess around with for maybe 30 minutes at a time, but gets repetative for longer periods.

This game is absolutely AWESOME!!! It's not just a game, it's a hacking simulation. Taking a computer security class and knowing Linux command line (which by the way, you should add "nano" or something like it for text editing), I flew through this game. I'm already rank 60 of 100 in CSEC and it's been fun the whole way through.

It's really fun to hack up the index.html's of websites, I went crazy on both CFC and DEC's site, but mostly CFC. I won't upload pictures of the hacked sites because I replaced the images with images that are most likely under copyright.

AND OH YEAH!!! This game is so realistic I can control my disc drive tray! lol, can't say that for much of any other digital download game. When the hacker with the proxy towards the beginning deleted my GUI, I went through the help pages and found openCDTray and closeCDTray
and since i was connected to my local machine and not a virtual character's machine, my disc tray would respond. So i commanded it to open and close a couple times and each time it closed it went through the normal process of seeing what disc was inserted (none).
a nice game for killing the time. teaches command line basics to linux newbies and enjoy it while learning at the same time.

Hacking for dummies, hacking 101 whatever you want to call it. Is a game where you investigate the death of BIT. As you progress you get to know about a few hacker communities which will help you progress further. They give you missions and while doing these missions you will gain new exe's to use to hack computers.

Something that i really like about this game is how they have been researching hacking and how terminals work. A newbeginner can easily pick this up and experienced users of command prompts and terminals can still pick this up and enjoy it. It's got some replay value with some stuff being randomly generated out of a pool of names etc... And in the future, the game will have multiplayer and mod support.

I say you get a lot for the price that is set and as it is summer sale right now as i am writing, i recommend that you give this game a go.

9/10 from me :D

Hacknet is an amazing experience. It's not too long (I finished the storyline in ~10 hours), but it's long enough. There are more missions, some of which are hidden, to further extend your playtime. 

Hacknet differs from many other hacking sims in that it's a terminal-based game which actually uses real commands. In addition, many of the programs you can use in-game, have real-world counterparts. This ups the realism and makes for an immersive experience. 

Also, the feeling you get after breaking into one of the more difficult servers is truly rewarding.

Hacknet has been an insanely fun game, it's very rare that you can buy a game and get addicted to it within the first hour of playing it. For those who dream of becoming a hacker but are too afraid to do it in real life... Hacknet is a satisfying game where you break into lots of computers, bypass security, and cover your tracks! I loved the detective aspect of the game, where it wouldn't "hold your hand" as you played. You would have to figure it out by looking around and making connections.

All in all, if you are still wondering whether or not to get the game: GET IT! Money well spent. I wish there was more, but I am completely satisfied that I got the "hacker" experience.
